This asset discount is further underscored by a reported P/B of 0.68x against a sector benchmark of 1.51x [E6]. Investors are being paid to wait through an attractive dividend yield of 8.83% [E3], backed by a strong multi-year top-line expansion featuring a compounded sales growth of 46% over 3 years [E13] and a recent year-over-year sales increase of 11% [E49]. Roadstar Infra Investment Trust carries fundamental operational flaws that make its low valuation a trap rather than a bargain. The trust posts a deeply negative P/E of -23.37x against a sector benchmark of 19.94x [E5], alongside a negative ROE of -6.83% which severely trails the sector benchmark of 4.82% [E8]. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted by -14% [E14], directly confirming that earnings growth is decelerating [E54]. Furthermore, price growth recently exceeds profit growth by 138%, demonstrating that market expectations are dangerously running ahead of actual delivery [E41]. Conceded: the dividend yield sits at an attractive 8.83% [E3] and the price-to-book ratio of 0.57x [E1] significantly discounts the book value of ₹ 106 [E1].

Conceded: the trailing twelve months compounded sales growth has contracted by -14% [E14], which aligns with decelerating earnings growth [E54]. However, the bear's focus on short-term contraction completely ignores the powerful 46% compounded sales growth achieved over the broader 3-year period [E13], proving fundamental business scale. The negative P/E of -23.37x [E5] and negative ROE of -6.83% [E8] fail to capture the true asset backing of the trust, given that the price-to-book ratio sits at a heavily discounted 0.57x against a book value of ₹ 106 [E1]. Furthermore, this 0.68x P/B valuation looks even more attractive when compared to the much higher sector benchmark of 1.51x [E6]. Finally, the bear's warning regarding price growth exceeding profit growth [E41] is neutralized by an exceptional 8.83% dividend yield [E3] that directly rewards investors while asset values normalize.

Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales growth is 46% [E13]. However, the bull's reliance on historical scale ignores the acute deterioration shown in the trailing twelve months compounded sales growth contraction of -14% [E14] alongside decelerating earnings growth [E54]. While the bull dismisses the negative P/E of -23.37x [E5] and negative ROE of -6.83% [E8] as mere artifacts ignoring asset backing, these metrics reflect real operational losses manifested in an ROA of -1.4% that severely trails the sector benchmark of 1.54% [E7]. The bull's defense of the 0.57x price-to-book ratio [E1] and sector-relative P/B [E6] fails to justify why the trust destroys shareholder equity at a -6.83% ROE [E8].
